title: What can you say about L-carnitine in your ads and on your site?
summary: The library supports 4 wordings for L-carnitine; the strongest is "Provides an antioxidant that helps protect cells against free radical damage" (moderate, up to 4 g a day). Avoid wording that names or implies a disease, a drug or a treatment, such as "Treats heart disease or angina".

supported_wordings.wording: Provides an antioxidant that helps protect cells against free radical damage.
supported_wordings.why: Health Canada lists it; no other listed source covers it.
supported_wordings.dose_details: Adults 18 and older. Health Canada: not more than 4 g a day; not more than 2 g per dose.
supported_wordings.form: L-carnitine, L-carnitine tartrate or L-carnitine fumarate, counted as L-carnitine

supported_wordings.wording: Helps support muscle recovery and muscle tissue repair in people doing resistance training.
supported_wordings.why: Health Canada lists it; no other listed source covers it.
supported_wordings.dose_details: Adults 18 and older. Health Canada: 1-4 g a day; not more than 2 g per dose. Take 2-4 hours before exercise.
supported_wordings.form: L-carnitine or L-carnitine tartrate, counted as L-carnitine

supported_wordings.wording: Helps improve physical performance and delay fatigue during physical activity, with a training regimen.
supported_wordings.why: Health Canada lists it; no other listed source covers it.
supported_wordings.dose_details: Adults 18 and older. Health Canada: 2-4 g a day; not more than 2 g per dose. Take 2-4 hours before exercise.
supported_wordings.form: L-carnitine or L-carnitine tartrate, counted as L-carnitine

supported_wordings.why: Health Canada lists it; no other listed source covers it.
supported_wordings.dose_details: Adults 18 and older. Health Canada: 3-4 g a day; not more than 2 g per dose.
supported_wordings.form: L-carnitine or L-carnitine tartrate, counted as L-carnitine

evidence_strengths.strong: At least two listed sources support it independently at a comparable dose and form, and none disagrees.
evidence_strengths.moderate: One listed source supports it as an evidence-based use at that dose, and no listed source disagrees.
evidence_strengths.limited: The only support is traditional use, the sources disagree, or the source itself calls the evidence weak.

reasons_to_avoid.drug: names a drug or presents the product as one
reasons_to_avoid.treatment: promises to treat, cure or prevent a condition

disclaimer: Not legal advice. This guide shows the wording that published evidence supports at a daily dose, from the sources linked below; it is not a ruling on any claim. Your own product, its form and dose, and your own evidence still need to match the wording you use.
